parameters.text:
=You score UK recruitment agencies as prospects for OpsAutomated, a managed AI automation service for small agencies (candidate inflow and screening built on their ATS). Return ONLY the JSON requested, no commentary.

ICP: UK recruitment agency, owner-led, 3-12 consultants (sub-20 staff), on an ATS, posting roles regularly. Niche agencies (tech, engineering, healthcare, finance) score higher. NOT an ICP: direct employers, large national agencies (Hays, Reed, Michael Page, Robert Walters, Adecco, Randstad, Manpower, Morgan McKinley, Noir, Opus, Sanderson and similar), umbrella companies, job boards, RPOs. An advertiser with 20+ live adverts is almost certainly too large.

STRONG SIGNALS, in order: hiring a resourcer, administrator or delivery consultant for its OWN desk (they are about to pay a person to handle inflow); high application counts on live adverts; several live roles at once; a small, long-standing company with one or two directors.
A [hiring_resourcer] advert only counts if it reads like the agency hiring for itself ("join our team", "we are a specialist agency", "our desk"). If it reads like a role recruited for a client, or the advertiser is a rec-to-rec firm, ignore it as a signal.

EVIDENCE
agency_id: {{ $json.agency_id }} (return this exact value in the JSON, unchanged)
Advertiser name: {{ $json.name }}
Companies House: {{ $json.ch_name || "no match" }} ({{ $json.company_number || "-" }}), incorporated {{ $json.incorporated_on || "-" }}, SIC {{ ($json.sic_codes || []).join(", ") || "unknown" }} (78109 = recruitment agency, 78200 = temp agency, 78300 = other HR provision)
Owner / longest-serving director: {{ $json.owner_name || "unknown" }} ({{ $json.owner_role || "-" }}), active directors: {{ $json.active_directors ?? "unknown" }}
Region: {{ $json.region || "-" }}
Live job adverts in the last 45 days: {{ $json.advert_count }}
Application counts: {{ ($json.adverts || []).some(x => x.applications !== null && x.applications !== undefined) ? ($json.total_applications + " in total across the adverts that report it") : "not available for these adverts (treat as unknown, not zero)" }}
{{ ($json.adverts || []).slice(0, 12).map(x => "- [" + x.type + "] " + x.detail).join("\n") }}

RULES
- Every field must be present and non-null. Strings you cannot determine are the exact string "unknown". Booleans are true or false. icp_score is a whole number 1-10. agency_id is copied exactly from the evidence.
- Missing data is unknown, never evidence against. Never penalise an agency for data that is not available, and never mention the absence of data or of a signal in why_now.
- is_agency: true only if the evidence says this is a recruitment agency (SIC 78xxx, "our client" language, agency-style name, or several roles across different employers). Direct employers get is_agency false and icp_score 1.
- icp_score 1-10: 9-10 agency plus a genuine own-desk resourcer hire or heavy application volume; 7-8 clearly a small agency (1-2 directors, SIC 78xxx) with two or more live roles; 5-6 agency with a single live role or thin evidence; 1-4 poor, unclear or too large.
- headcount_band: one of "1-2", "3-12", "13-20", "20+", "unknown". Infer from directors, company age, advert volume and tone. One director and a handful of roles is usually 3-12, not 1-2.
- vertical: one or two words (tech, engineering, healthcare, finance, construction, generalist) or "unknown".
- why_now: maximum 40 words. An OBSERVATION about this agency's live roles only: what they are hiring for, where, how many, application volume if known, an own-desk resourcer hire if there is one. Positive facts only. Never a pitch, never mention automation, screening, saving time or OpsAutomated. Example: "Hiring a resourcer in Chelmsford while running four live .NET roles, two of them past 60 applications."
- disqualify: true if is_agency is false or this is a large agency.
- reason: one sentence on the evidence you used.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample:
{
  "agency_id": "1135f0f0-157f-449f-9929-f2eb17feaab1",
  "is_agency": true,
  "icp_score": 8,
  "vertical": "tech",
  "headcount_band": "3-12",
  "why_now": "Hiring a resourcer in Chelmsford while running four live .NET roles, two of them past 60 applications.",
  "disqualify": false,
  "reason": "SIC 78109, our-client language in adverts, incorporated 2019."
}

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_agency_id: $json.output.agency_id, p_icp_score: Number($json.output.icp_score) || 1, p_why_now: String($json.output.why_now || '').split(/\s+/).slice(0, 40).join(' '), p_vertical: $json.output.vertical || null, p_headcount_band: $json.output.headcount_band || null, p_disqualify: $json.output.disqualify === true || $json.output.is_agency === false }) }}

parameters.content:
## BD - Signals v1
Reed adverts → Supabase ops.agencies / ops.signals → Companies House → Sonnet ICP score.

Writes go through SQL functions (ingest_signal, enrich_agency, score_agency, agencies_to_score) so dedupe and status rules live in the database, not here.

Change the search in Config. ATS detection is parked: Reed URLs never reveal the ATS; needs the agency website.

nodeGroups.name: 1. Collect
nodeGroups.description: Reed Jobseeker API, agencies only: tech roles and resourcer/admin roles, one signal per advert with its application count

nodeGroups.name: 2. Enrich
nodeGroups.description: Companies House number, SIC codes, incorporation date, owner (longest-serving active director), active director count

nodeGroups.name: 3. Score
nodeGroups.description: Sonnet ICP score 1-10, headcount band, vertical and a 40-word why-now, saved to ops.agencies as status scored
